**Finding submitted: deviation (high severity, LD rule).**

**What I found.** The agreement contains no clause using the words "liquidated damages" or "penalty" against us, but Section 4.2 (¶p0026) operates as one: on *any* Company termination we must pay HDI a "Termination Payment" equal to (trailing 12-month Net Sales − $800,000) ÷ 2.

**Why it fails the fallback.** Our fees under Section 3.1 are 30% of Net Sales above $11,000/month, so the termination formula (50% of Net Sales above $800,000) can exceed a full year of fees — far more than the fallback's three-months'-fees cap, and more than the remaining contract value given the one-year auto-renewing term terminable on 90 days' notice. It also bites even where we terminate for HDI's default; the only "without penalty" exit is the narrow launch-failure right in Section 1.6 (¶p0011). Sections 4.2(b)–(c) (no payment if the formula is ≤ zero; eight quarterly instalments) mitigate cash-flow but not the exposure.

**Redline (validated, ok:true).** Rather than delete the payment outright — HDI's site build-out investment is the core bargain here, so preferred deletion is disproportionate — I took the fallback with a single minimal insertion into ¶p0026: cap the Termination Payment at fees paid in the three months preceding the Termination Date, and disapply it where we terminate for HDI's breach.
